description: A table of rules (a DMN decision table of a solution, rules/<name>.dmn, listed under decisions). A decide step asks it and keeps what its first matching row says; a workflow's policy judges each command its steps send. One row per case, readable by somebody who is not a developer.

rules: One decision per file; its id is the key workflows name it by (rules: of a decide step, policy: of a workflow)
hitPolicy FIRST: the first row that fits answers; no row fitting gives an empty answer, and NEEDS_APPROVAL from a policy
Each input looks at a value of the case by its name (an expression without ${}), such as order.total or operation
Say it in words: a description of the decision (what the rules are for), of the table (what comes of no row fitting), of each input (where the value comes from) and of each row (why)

cells.any: an empty cell or - fits any value
cells.value: one value: "text" in double quotes, a number, true or false
cells.refused: Several values with commas between them ("a","b") cannot be read by the engine, and a row it cannot read stops the whole table: give each value a row of its own

policy.description: The rules a workflow's commands are judged by (policy: of the workflow). They look at what the command does and the case, and answer verdict.

inputs.connector: the connection the command goes to
inputs.operation: what it asks the connection to do, such as message.send
inputs.<variable>: anything the case worked out or read

outputsBesides.decides: a role of People that decides this action, instead of the workflow's whoDecides

policy.rule: Every command the workflow can send has a row. Start strict (NEEDS_APPROVAL) and loosen with what test runs show.
